title: Which CompTIA Certification Should You Take First?
excerpt: A+, Network+, Security+ or CySA+? Here's a simple path through CompTIA's core certifications.
description: A+, Network+, Security+ or CySA+? A simple guide to the order most people take CompTIA certifications, and what each one proves.
body:
CompTIA certifications are vendor-neutral, so they're recognised by employers around the world. If you're not sure where to start, this is the path most people follow.

## 1. CompTIA A+

A+ is the starting point for IT support roles. It has two exams: Core 1 covers hardware, mobile devices, networking and troubleshooting, and Core 2 covers operating systems, security and operational procedures. You need to pass both.

## 2. CompTIA Network+

Network+ proves you can set up, manage and troubleshoot networks. It's a natural next step after A+, and a strong base for any security role.

## 3. CompTIA Security+

Security+ is the most popular entry-level cybersecurity certification. Many employers list it as a requirement for security jobs.

## 4. CompTIA CySA+

CySA+ is an intermediate certification for security analysts. It focuses on detecting threats, managing vulnerabilities and responding to incidents.

## Can you skip ahead?

Yes. CompTIA doesn't force you to take exams in order. If you already work in IT, you might start with Network+ or Security+. Just make sure you're comfortable with the basics each exam assumes.

## How to prepare

- Download the official exam objectives and use them as your checklist
- Study one domain at a time
- Take timed practice exams and focus on your weakest domains
- Book the exam when you score 85% or more consistently
